recipes.name: Savory Tater Tot Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (19 ounce) can cream of chicken soup

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Lightly coat a 9x13-inch glass baking dish with cooking spray.

Spread ground beef over the bottom of the prepared baking dish, gently pressing it into an even layer. Sprinkle onion over beef. Layer frozen mixed vegetables evenly on top, then spread cream of chicken soup evenly over vegetables.

Arrange potato tots in an even layer on top. Bake in the preheated oven until potato tots are golden brown and an instant-read thermometer inserted into the beef layer reads at least 160 degrees F (71 degrees C), about 1 hour. Check after 30 minutes; if potato tots are getting too brown, reduce the oven temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Savory Tater Tot Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This easy beef Tater Tot casserole layers ground beef, mixed vegetables, creamy chicken soup, and crispy potato tots for a simple one-pan dinner.

review.reviewBody: I tried everything that this recipe called for,except I put a little twist in this dish...with a little help from my boyfriend who happens to have at least four years restaurant exp.I used one teaspoon of onion powder,a teaspoon of garlic powder,one package of Lipton onion soup mix,and of course can't forget one twelve ounce bottle of chili sauce,and two tablespoons of Worchestersire sauce.I combined all of these ingredients into the ground beef after browning the meat,then I layered it on the bottom of the casserole dish.Then I added all the mixed veggies,layered with shredded chedder cheese,then two cans of cream of celery soup and then I topped it all off with one bag of tator tots.I cooked this dish at 350 degrees for 25 minutes.

This is an okay basic recipe, but I browned the ground beef first, then mixed in 1/2 envelope of Lipton Onion Soup Mix and 2 medium cloves of minced garlic (I am a garlic lover). I put the beef mixture in the bottom of the dish, then layered canned French cut green beans and canned corn (both drained thoroughly). I can't stand cream of chicken soup, so I mixed a can of cream of mushroom with a can of cheddar cheese soup and poured half the mixture over the meat and veggies. Then I added the tater tots on top and spread the remaining soup mixture over that and baked. Husband loved it!

Like others mentioned, I cooked my ground beef first and added 2 cloves of garlic and 1/2 package of onion soup mix to the meat. I added a can of corn and a can of French cut beans, then spread 2 cans of cream of mushroom soup over that. I added my tots (I had exactly enough) and put in the oven. After about 25 min, I turned the heat up to 425 seeing how I didn't have to cook the hamburger. Then, I covered the tots with shredded medium cheddar cheese and put back in the oven for 20 min. The cheese looked nice and crispy, so I took it out of the oven. Served with French fried onions and sour cream. Sooooooo good!

Ahhh the recipe I grew up with as a kid in the 70s and 80s! Nostalgia abounds! A couple of minor changes that people have mentioned. 1st season the ground beef and cook it first, then drain it before putting in the 9x13. I use McCormick Hamburger seasoning or Montreal Steak seasoning. The seasoning is a must. Cooking and draining helps reduce getting a fat pool at the bottom of the pan if you just put the raw meat in. Also I used a shallot ofr the onion which gives a milder flavor profile if someone isn't a fan of onion. Then once you put on the tots sprinkle a little Lawrys seasoning salt, just a bit. Cook for 30 minutes then take out and put shredded cheese then back in for another 20-30 minutes.

Here I am changing up the recipe! 🙂. I used rotisserie chicken with the cream of chicken soup, added a little bit of Mrs. Dash, onion powder, and garlic powder and after 30 minutes I added some shredded cheddar and left it in the oven for another 10. Loved it.

I like the ingredients in this recipe, except I use cream of mushroom soup instead of chicken. I also cook the ground beef with the onions, season well, and then add the soup and veggies and heat through. This cuts down the oven time immensely. Only need to brown the tator tots and it is done!!

This recipe is super easy, especially during the weeknights when cooking is such a hassle. I made a few small changes, which were suggested by another reviewer. 

I browned the ground beef and onions ahead of time, and seasoned to taste with garlic salt, sea salt, and onion powder. I try to stay away from anything with MSG, yeast extract, or similar additives; so I use Pacific brand cream of chicken soup. Otherwise, I stuck to the main ingredients.

Since I browned the beef ahead of time, that cut the cooking time almost in half. I baked it uncovered for 35 minutes at 350 degrees. I then put it under the broiler for about 5 minutes since we like the tater tots to be crispy. Everyone loved it, which is quite an accomplishment!

Thanks for the recipe!

After reading the recipe I had reservation and scrolled down to see the reviews. I too couldn't start with raw ground beef. I browned it first and added salt and pepper. You really need to cook the beef first. The canned soup seemed to linger on the top. Hindsight I recommend combining the frozen veggies and soup together and forming that as one layer. Lastly, when I pulled the casserole out of the oven it looked nekked. I sprinkled cheese over the top and stuck it in 5 minutes longer. It needs the cheese in my opinion. Overall good recipe but needs tweaks. I can only give it 3 stars as written.

I used 1 can of mix vegetables & 1 can of corn. I browned the beef with onion, and seasoned with onion powder, pepper, and nature seasons. In large mixing bowl, I mixed 1 can cream of celery, 1 can cream of chicken, 1 soup can of milk, vegetables, big dash of Worcestershire, shredded cheddar cheese, season and mix. Add drained hamburger, mix well. Baked in metal 9x13 cake pan at 350 covered w/foil for 35 minutes. Uncovered, raised temperature to 375 and baked another 20 minutes. Very good, will make again

2 stars before tweaking it. As it reads, it clearly lacks flavor or seasoning. I cook the meat ahead with onion, garlic, worcestershire, an envelope of beefy onion soup mix, a little ketchup, onion and garlic powder. The veggies need a little salt. I use cream of mushroom soup then a couple of cups of shredded cracker barrel cheddar, and top with ore ida extra crispy tots. Sometimes, I only use canned green beans and corn instead of the frozen mixed veggies. If using the canned veggies, I dont add salt to them. Lightly salt the tots when it comes out of the oven. You would do that if you were having them any other way. If they aren't crispy enough, turn on the broiler for a minute or two. My grandchildren give it 10 stars. LOL

I browned the ground beef and onions together and drained off the fat, then added the frozen mixed vegetables and one can of cream of chicken soup. I poured it all in a casserole dish and topped it with the tater tots. Baked it for 30 minutes and it was perfect. It is a quick dish to make and has everything in it for a good dinner, fast! I have already made it twice.

Turned out fine. I added adobo seasoning to the meat and vegetables, and I put cheese on top towards the end. It’s definitely missing something though. I think I’ll add some more seasonings to the meat next time, as well as mix the soup and vegetables together with seasonings before adding it to the dish. Other than that, very easy to make and definitely edible.

The potato were nice and crispy, but the onion and veggies were too crisp. Next time I will micro wave the veggies a little first with onion and use cream of mushroom soup. Finally, add some Trader Joes Mushroom and company seasoning.
I added taco seasoning to my meat

This was really, really good! I cooked the meat ahead of time, but found that by doing so made the meat a bit too dry. When I make it again I will keep the meat raw. I used cream of mushroom soup. I added frozen peas, frozen corn and mushrooms with Colby Jack cheese on top. My brother said it was a bit bland so may want to add some salt and some other herbs/spices as desired. I ate leftovers yesterday and added sour cream and ketchup on top. Will definitely be making this again!
Never made a tater tot casserole. But this was a great spin on shepherd’s pie or cottage pie. I always add my favorite seasonings.

As previously suggested, I cooked the meat and mixed in onion soup mix. I also spread shredded cheddar over the soup. The tots were perfect after 30 minutes. My husband really liked it, although the combination of soups made it a little salty.
It was okay next time I'm gonna add some spices to the ground beef because it was bland otherwise
